# Zapier's AI Updates: What They Mean for Your Daily Work

> **In short:** Zapier has folded its former AI helper, Zapier Agents, into a single AI step inside the regular Zap editor, and has added Google's Gemini models as an option you can plug into any AI step in a workflow.

If you've ever wished one of your apps could just handle a small task while you sleep, Zapier is one of the names that comes up. It's a tool that connects different apps — think Gmail, Google Sheets, Slack, a calendar — so that when something happens in one, something else can happen automatically in another. The two updates below both make that "something else" smarter, in slightly different ways.

## The first update: one AI step, inside every Zap

Zapier says that what used to be a separate product called Zapier Agents — its stand-alone AI helper — has now been folded directly into the regular Zap editor as a single **AI by Zapier** step. In plain terms: instead of going off to a separate corner of Zapier to set up an "agent," you just drop one AI block into the workflow you were already building.

According to Zapier, that AI step carries over the same four capabilities the old Agents product had:

- **A prompt** — the instruction you give the AI, like "summarize this email in two sentences"
- **A set of tools** — other Zapier actions the AI is allowed to use, such as "send a Slack message" or "create a Calendar event"
- **A trigger** — the event that starts the whole thing, such as "a new email arrives in Gmail"
- **Permission to act** — the AI is allowed to do those things on your behalf, not just suggest them

So if you used Zapier Agents before, Zapier says the new AI step does the same job — it just lives in the same place as the rest of your workflow, which is a smaller change to navigate than learning a whole separate screen.

## The second update: Gemini is now an option inside Zapier

The second announcement is about Google's **Gemini** family of AI models. Gemini is the name Google uses for its chatbots and the AI models behind them — different versions are meant for quick replies versus longer, more careful thinking.

Zapier says Google's Gemini models are now available to plug into an AI step in a Zap. In practice, this means when you set up an AI block in a workflow, Gemini is one of the model choices you can pick. According to Zapier, this matters because sometimes you don't need the most powerful model — you need the cheapest, fastest one that can handle a 50-word summary. And sometimes you do want a more capable model to work through a tangled customer email.

## What this means for you

- **If you're new to Zapier**: Think of Zapier as a way to chain small jobs together. The new AI step is one of those small jobs — it can read something, decide what to do, and then do it. You don't need to learn a separate "Agents" product anymore. One block, in one place.
- **If you already use Zapier**: The biggest practical change is where you click. Anything you used to do inside Zapier Agents is now an AI step inside the regular Zap editor — open any Zap, drop the AI step in, give it a prompt, hand it the apps it can use, and let it run.
- **If you care about which AI model does the work**: According to Zapier, the new AI step lets you pick which model runs it, and Gemini is now one of the choices. That matters when a quick summary needs a cheap, fast model, while a long, tangled email benefits from a more capable one. The same Zap can even use different models in different steps.

## Wrap-up

Both updates point in the same direction: smarter building blocks, in fewer places. The one thing to remember is this — Zapier now has an AI step you can drop into any workflow, and you can choose Google's Gemini family as the engine for that step. A next step to try today: open a Zap you've already built, add an AI step, and give it a prompt you already find yourself writing by hand — chances are, that's the exact job it's meant to take off your plate.
